questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In a full 4-ary tree (every internal node has exactly 4 children) with 7 internal nodes, how many leaf nodes are there?
questions.explanationEn: For a full k-ary tree with I internal nodes, the number of leaves is L = (k - 1)I + 1 = (4 - 1)(7) + 1 = 22.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which data structure is used internally by a runtime system to manage function call activation records (return addresses and local variables)?
questions.explanationEn: Function calls follow Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) semantics: the most recently called function must finish and return before its caller resumes, matching a call stack.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about open addressing in hash tables are TRUE?
optionsEn: The load factor α = n/m can never exceed 1
Deleting an element requires placing a special tombstone (deleted) marker rather than simply marking the slot empty
Quadratic probing always guarantees visiting every slot in the table for any table size m
questions.explanationEn: Open addressing stores all keys inside the table so α <= 1 (A), lazy deletion uses tombstones so probe chains don't break (B), and double hashing varies step sizes per key to avoid primary clustering (C). Quadratic probing only visits all slots under specific table sizes/constants (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In a singly linked list with only a `head` pointer (no `tail` pointer), what is the worst-case time complexity to delete the last node of a list with `n` nodes?
questions.explanationEn: Deleting the last node requires updating the `next` pointer of the second-to-last node to `NULL`, which requires traversing all n - 1 nodes from `head` in O(n) time.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Given a pointer `p` directly to a middle node of a doubly linked list, what is the time complexity to delete node `p`?
questions.explanationEn: In a doubly linked list, `p->prev` and `p->next` are directly accessible, so unlinking `p` takes just two pointer updates in O(1) time.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Keys 22, 33, 44, 55, 12 are inserted in that order into an empty hash table of size 11 using hash function h(k) = k mod 11 and linear probing. At which slot index (0 to 10) is key 12 placed?
questions.explanationEn: 22 mod 11 = 0 -> slot 0. 33 mod 11 = 0 -> probe to slot 1. 44 mod 11 = 0 -> probe to slot 2. 55 mod 11 = 0 -> probe to slot 3. 12 mod 11 = 1 -> slots 1, 2, 3 are occupied, so 12 is placed at slot 4.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A 10 × 10 lower-triangular matrix stores only elements `A[i][j]` with `i >= j` consecutively in a 1D array. How many elements are stored in the 1D array?
questions.explanationEn: Number of stored elements = 1 + 2 + ... + 10 = 10 × 11 / 2 = 55.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following operations can be performed in O(1) worst-case time?
optionsEn: Inserting a node at the head of a singly linked list
Finding the maximum element in a binary max-heap
Checking if an edge (u, v) exists in an adjacency matrix
Deleting the maximum element from a binary max-heap
questions.explanationEn: Head insertion in a linked list, reading `heap[0]` in a max-heap, and indexing `M[u][v]` in an adjacency matrix are all O(1). Deleting the max from a heap requires `Heapify`, taking O(log n) (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A hash table has 12 buckets using separate chaining. If 60 keys are inserted into the table, what is the average chain length (load factor)?
questions.explanationEn: Load factor α = n / m = 60 / 12 = 5.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A B-tree of order `m = 5` (maximum 5 children and 4 keys per node) has height `h = 2` (root at level 0, internal nodes at level 1, leaves at level 2). What is the MINIMUM number of keys in this B-tree?
questions.explanationEn: Minimum keys: Root has at least 1 key (2 children at level 1). Each level-1 node has at least `ceil(5/2) - 1 = 2` keys and `ceil(5/2) = 3` children -> `2 × 3 = 6` leaves at level 2. Each leaf has at least 2 keys -> `6 × 2 = 12` keys. Total = `1 + (2×2) + 12 = 1 + 4 + 12 = 17` keys.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: The preorder traversal of a Binary Search Tree is: `30, 20, 10, 25, 40, 35, 50`. What is its postorder traversal?
questions.explanationEn: Root is 30. Left subtree has `{20, 10, 25}` -> root 20, left 10, right 25 -> postorder `10, 25, 20`. Right subtree has `{40, 35, 50}` -> root 40, left 35, right 50 -> postorder `35, 50, 40`. Combined postorder: `10, 25, 20, 35, 50, 40, 30`.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the max-heap stored in array `[90, 75, 80, 50, 60, 40, 70]`. After performing one `Extract-Max` operation, what is the resulting array?
questions.explanationEn: Replace root 90 with last element 70: `[70, 75, 80, 50, 60, 40]`. Children of 70 are 75 and 80; swap 70 with larger child 80 -> `[80, 75, 70, 50, 60, 40]`. Now 70's only child is 40 (< 70), so heap property is restored.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Programming & Data Structures (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements comparing AVL trees and Red-Black trees are TRUE?
optionsEn: Both AVL trees and Red-Black trees guarantee O(log n) worst-case height
AVL trees are more strictly balanced than Red-Black trees, resulting in faster lookups on average
Inserting a key into an AVL tree requires at most one single or double rotation to restore balance
Deleting a key from an AVL tree always requires at most one rotation
questions.explanationEn: Both have O(log n) height (A), AVL has tighter height bound (~1.44 log n vs 2 log n) aiding lookups (B), and AVL insertion fixes imbalance with at most 1 rotation (single or double) (C). Deletion in an AVL tree may propagate up the root requiring O(log n) rotations (D is false).
